metadata.task: If the bookshelf contains misplaced books, organize them; otherwise arrange the magazines on the coffee table.

plan.goal: Organize misplaced books on the bookshelf or arrange magazines on the coffee table, depending on which condition holds.

checkpoints.checkpoint_goal: Verify the state of the bookshelf (misplaced books) and the coffee table (magazines) to determine the correct execution path.
checkpoints.entry_state: Robot at initial spawn location. Bookshelf and Coffee Table exist. Contents unknown.
checkpoints.exit_state: Robot has detected the bookshelf and coffee table. Robot has identified the objects on them. Robot has determined if books are misplaced or if magazines need arranging.

actions.action: Inspect the bookshelf to detect books.
Analyze the arrangement of books to determine if they are misplaced.
Inspect the coffee table to detect magazines.
Analyze the arrangement of magazines to determine if they need organizing.

grounded_skills.reason: Robot must move to the bookshelf to inspect it.
Robot must perceive the books on the bookshelf.
Robot must analyze the scene to determine if books are misplaced.
Robot must move to the coffee table to inspect it.
Robot must perceive the magazines on the coffee table.
Robot must analyze the scene to determine if magazines need arranging.

constraints: Robot cannot climb stairs or walk; must use wheeled navigation.
Robot cannot fly or swim; environment is indoor residential.
Robot has single arm only; cannot use two hands simultaneously.
Robot cannot assemble or disassemble objects directly; relies on manipulation skills like pick/place/arrange.

execution_summary.expected_outcome: Based on the inspection results from Checkpoint 1, the robot will branch to either organize the books on the bookshelf (if misplaced) or arrange the magazines on the coffee table (if needed). This decision logic is encapsulated in the conditional task structure.
